ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Program-level exposure to missile, radar, electronic-warfare, classified, rotary-wing, fixed-wing, and space platforms; evidence of supplier awards, sole-source status, long qualification cycles, customer-funded capacity, backlog pull-through, and pass-through funding from primes or government programs.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need primary-source confirmation from filings, investor presentations, contract announcements, earnings transcripts, or customer disclosures that specific defense programs are driving backlog, pricing, margins, or funded capacity.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Ducommun is the best fit for the Serenity Layer 3 funnel because it combines a low-attention public-market profile with plausible exposure to qualified aerospace and defense electronics, structures, engineered products, assemblies, missile, radar, classified, space, rotary-wing, and fixed-wing programs. The broader evidence base supports a thesis that lower-tier defense suppliers can become bottlenecks when DoD and primes lack visibility beyond tier two, while procurement demand alone cannot rapidly create qualified production capacity.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: It is not a prime contractor or high-profile defense-tech company. Its exposure is embedded in assemblies, structures, manufacturing services, and electronics that screen as industrial aerospace rather than as direct politics or defense-budget beneficiaries.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Whether Park materials are qualified into specific missile, rocket motor, radome, UAV, strategic-weapons, military-aircraft, tactical-motor, engine, or space-launch programs where qualification cycles, domestic sourcing, or capacity limits are material.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need direct evidence tying Park's materials to named defense programs, customer concentration, qualification scarcity, capacity utilization, pricing power, or customer-funded expansion.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Park Aerospace scores highly because it is a small-cap, low-attention materials supplier with plausible exposure to qualified aerospace composites, radomes, UAVs, rocket motors, tactical motors, strategic weapons, military aircraft, and space launch. Materials qualification, domestic sourcing, and limited supplier redundancy can create bottlenecks several tiers below the prime contractors.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: It is primarily labeled as an aerospace composites/materials company rather than a defense-industrial-base chokepoint. Its possible defense signal is hidden in qualified materials and program-specific applications rather than headline contract awards.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Whether Government & Defense test systems are tied to funded modernization programs, production test bottlenecks, munitions/electronics test capacity, FAA/ODA certification gates, military-aircraft support, or aircraft sustainment programs.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need segment-level evidence showing that defense test systems or certification-related programs are driving backlog, margin improvement, customer awards, or capacity constraints rather than merely benefiting from broad aerospace recovery.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Astronics is prioritized because test systems, certification, power, connectivity, and aircraft support can become second-order bottlenecks when defense modernization, aircraft sustainment, electronics content, and production ramp requirements rise. The candidate has a testable path through Government & Defense test-system orders and certification-related demand.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: Its market identity is mixed across commercial aerospace recovery, cabin systems, power, connectivity, lighting, aircraft structures, and test systems. That mixed label may obscure narrower defense test-system and certification bottleneck exposure.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Whether backlog and bookings are tied to specific munitions, radar, electronic-warfare, missile-defense, aircraft, naval, or space programs where electronics supply is a schedule bottleneck.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need program-level bookings/backlog evidence and margin evidence showing that Mercury is benefiting from scarcity or trusted-supplier status rather than simply participating in broad defense electronics demand.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Mercury is a strong reference anchor for tier-2 defense electronics, mission processing, embedded computing, RF, and sensor-processing subsystems. It maps directly onto the policy and technology thesis that electronics content, open systems, radar, EW, missiles, aircraft, naval, and space programs may expose lower-tier constraints.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: It is more visible than the underfollowed small and mixed-label suppliers, so it is less of a discovery candidate. However, it remains below the prime-contractor attention layer and is useful for mapping trusted defense-electronics bottlenecks.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Government revenue durability, military contract vehicles, military aircraft platform exposure, parts-distribution margins, mobility/pallet demand, DoD sustainment awards, and whether readiness spending is driving incremental backlog.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need clearer primary-source split between commercial aviation recovery and defense/government readiness pull-through, including contract duration, margin profile, and backlog contribution.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: AAR ranks ahead of larger reference names because sustainment, aircraft parts distribution, MRO, expeditionary support, and readiness logistics are plausible second-order beneficiaries of defense policy and operating-tempo increases. Sustainment bottlenecks may be less visible than new-platform procurement but can matter when readiness targets and flight-hour activity rise.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: AAR is usually viewed as aviation services, distribution, and MRO rather than as a direct defense-spending or politics beneficiary. Its government and readiness exposure may be hidden inside parts availability, logistics, and sustainment workflows.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Defense-specific revenue mix, titanium/nickel alloy capacity, domestic supply-chain qualification, long-term agreements with engine and airframe OEMs, and whether DoD reshoring or critical-mineral rules improve pricing or volume.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need clearer defense-specific exposure and evidence that policy or supply-chain constraints are changing ATI's volumes, pricing, utilization, or customer-funded capacity, rather than broader aerospace-cycle demand.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: ATI is a plausible second-order defense-industrial-base materials candidate because qualified titanium, nickel alloys, superalloys, specialty steels, and domestic/allied materials capacity can sit several tiers below primes and constrain aircraft, engines, naval, and missile-related supply chains.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: It is not obscure by market cap, but the defense chokepoint angle may be under-mapped because ATI screens as specialty materials rather than as a defense supplier. Materials constraints can be hidden deep in the supply chain.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Whether smaller suppliers show similar program pull-through, backlog growth, or qualification scarcity in the same naval, aircraft, power-system, and electronics submarkets.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need to determine whether the incremental alpha is already broadly recognized in valuation and sell-side coverage, and whether smaller suppliers offer purer or more mispriced exposure.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Curtiss-Wright has strong relevance as a scaled benchmark for qualified defense components, electronics, naval, aerospace, and power-system exposure. It is useful for mapping the chokepoint thesis but is less compelling as a discovery candidate because it is larger and more recognized.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: It is less underfollowed than the small/mid-cap subtier candidates. Its role in this chunk is primarily as a reference anchor for qualified defense-component exposure.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Defense backlog by platform, exposure to missiles and space, organic growth in defense controls, and whether customers are funding capacity or qualification work.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need primary-source evidence that defense controls or actuation are capacity-constrained and that Moog has pricing power, customer-funded expansion, or program-specific backlog growth tied to defense policy demand.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Moog is a useful reference-map candidate for qualified motion controls, actuation, flight controls, propulsion controls, missile controls, naval controls, and space controls. Long qualification cycles and mission-critical reliability can create scarcity, but the candidate is less underfollowed than smaller subtier names.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: Moog is less visible than prime contractors but not a low-attention small-cap. Its defense signal may be partially hidden by diversified aerospace and industrial exposure.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Actual non-Chinese feedstock-qualified NdFeB magnet production, DoD contract terms, pricing floors, customer qualification milestones, and whether waivers delay or accelerate demand.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need confirmation that policy support converts into economically attractive, qualified, scaled magnet production and that defense or allied sourcing requirements create durable demand rather than a well-known policy narrative already priced by the market.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: MP Materials has a clear thematic connection to rare earths, NdFeB magnets, non-Chinese supply chains, domestic-content rules, and defense critical-mineral policy. However, it ranks lower in this underfollowed-discovery funnel because it is high-attention and the key thesis depends on verifying actual qualified magnet production, customer qualification milestones, and DoD contract economics.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: It is not underfollowed. It is included as a reference anchor for rare-earth and magnet supply-chain policy risk, not as the main small/mid-cap discovery target.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Defense/government revenue exposure, military platform support, contract vehicles, parts availability bottlenecks, margin impact from inventory, and whether readiness budgets are creating incremental demand.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: The current evidence does not yet prove that defense readiness or government sustainment demand is material enough to drive VSEC earnings, backlog, pricing, or margins. Next verification should use VSEC filings, segment revenue disclosures, contract announcements, government award databases, and earnings-call language around defense, government, readiness, and parts availability.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: VSEC is prioritized because the defense-readiness and aviation-sustainment angle is a plausible second-order beneficiary of higher defense utilization, readiness budgets, parts availability needs, and aftermarket support demand. The thesis is less dependent on proving a single-source chokepoint and more dependent on verifiable public disclosures: government revenue mix, defense contract vehicles, platform support, parts distribution growth, inventory turns, margins, and backlog/order indicators. This makes the candidate more falsifiable than Gabler while still fitting the underfollowed-discovery lens because it may screen as a commercial aviation aftermarket services company rather than a defense readiness beneficiary.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: May be categorized by investors and screens as aviation aftermarket distribution, MRO, fleet, or commercial services rather than as a defense-industrial-base readiness and sustainment beneficiary.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Correct listing ticker, audited filings, revenue/backlog, customer concentration, single-source claims, order backlog quality, margins, free float, liquidity, and whether submarine-program exposure is real and material.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: The candidate currently rests on promotional or secondary context rather than validated primary evidence. Before promotion, research must confirm the legal entity, exchange listing, ticker, audited financials, defense/submarine revenue materiality, actual customers or programs, backlog quality, free float, liquidity, and whether any claimed single-source position is documented.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Gabler is retained only as a speculative shadow candidate because the alleged niche submarine and subsea hardware exposure would be highly aligned with European defense rearmament, naval readiness, and scarce subtier supplier themes if validated. Its potential underfollowed value comes from being obscure, possibly newly listed, and outside standard defense screens. However, it ranks below VSEC because the primary facts needed to establish public-market investability, revenue materiality, audited financials, customer concentration, backlog, and single-source relevance are not yet validated.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: Appears to be a niche European submarine or subsea hardware supplier with little or no conventional analyst attention, unclear listing details, and potentially messy public-market visibility.
